extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys and agents, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and respondents in USPTO reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order imposing reciprocal suspension of a patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court suspension, describing the procedural steps, regulatory authorities invoked, the professional-conduct violations relied upon, and the administrative relief ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of OED filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting identical discipline to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Illinois; action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may base reciprocal discipline on a practitioner's state suspension; the Final Order suspends respondent for violating § 11.804(h) predicated on the Illinois suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose reciprocal discipline (Notice and response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be served and provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt numbers provided) and delivered; respondent had 40 days to respond but did not file a response. Responses can be based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting reciprocal discipline (no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, it may be determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and reciprocal suspension identical to the state discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states that, in light of respondent's failure to respond, no genuine issue exists and suspension for sixty (60) days is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline on the grounds enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice referenced § 11.24(d)(1) as providing the available reasons to oppose; although the specific reasons are not restated in this document, they are the regulatory grounds for challenging reciprocity (e.g., procedural defects, lack of due process, disparity in facts or punishment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the text of the 'NOTICE OF SUSPENSION' to be published, identifying the practitioner, registration number, scope of suspension (patent, trademark, non-patent matters), the predicate rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), the underlying state disciplinary findings, and that action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs OED to provide the notices required by § 11.59 as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of a disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner is required to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly requires the respondent to comply with § 11.58 duties (though it does not restate them here); OED will enforce those obligations during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the administrative relief, the practitioner’s access and identity in USPTO electronic systems are to be dissociated to prevent practice before the Office during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents the disciplined practitioner from practicing before the USPTO electronically during the suspension period and until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis in State professional conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State rules of professional conduct may form the factual basis for reciprocal discipline (here, Illinois Rules cited: 1.3; 1.4(a)(3); 8.1(a); 8.4(c); 8.4(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Illinois Supreme Court suspended the respondent for violating these Illinois Rules; the USPTO invoked those state findings as the predicate for federal reciprocal discipline. The Order lists the specific Illinois Rules that were found violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct supporting suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific acts identified that supported the Illinois suspension include failing to timely file a patent application and failing to timely file a complaint in a civil proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete failures to act (lack of diligence/timeliness) were cited as examples of conduct demonstrating violations of the professional-conduct rules (e.g., Rule 1.3, Rule 1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct categories: false statements and dishonesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Misconduct that can support discipline includes making a statement of material fact known by the lawyer to be false in connection with a lawyer disciplinary matter, and engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (Illinois Rules 8.1(a) and 8.4(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these categories as among the grounds on which the state suspended the practitioner and which the USPTO relied upon for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct category: conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct which is prejudicial to the administration of justice (Illinois Rule 8.4(d)) can support suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state court found this violation among others; the USPTO's reciprocal discipline references it as part of the factual predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation requirement (35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal disciplinary actions are taken pursuant to statutory authority, here cited as 35 U.S.C. § 32 in addition to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states that the action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, establishing the statutory/regulatory basis for the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative relief is not limited (catch-all for further relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order may include 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language reserves authority to impose additional administrative measures beyond those enumerated, as necessary to effectuate discipline.
